reflections.summary: The 1-2 series loss was decided in game 3 by failing to convert an excellent turn-1 Charizard knockout into a stable Trick Room endgame. Farigiraf’s turn-1 flinch delayed Trick Room, Camerupt was heavily damaged before it could function, and Excadrill’s repeated Earthquakes controlled the board. The eventual Trick Room position did not help because Camerupt entered at 47% directly into Earthquake and was KOed before attacking; Mega Mawile then could not finish Focus Sash Excadrill. The Mega Mawile adjustment supplied Intimidate and immediate pressure, but it was poorly suited to the final Excadrill-centric position because both Mawile and Camerupt were highly vulnerable to Earthquake. The four brought had a sound anti-Charizard lead in Farigiraf/Heliolisk, but lacked a durable way to preserve or capitalize on Trick Room against Excadrill. Preparation correctly included Farigiraf, Heliolisk, and Trick Room Mega Camerupt options for Charizard and speed control, but overcommitting three Mega options in the six did not clearly improve this matchup. Tauros was the only registered non-Mega alternative left unused; the supplied evidence does not establish that any unregistered Pokémon or unseen set would definitely have been better.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain the Farigiraf/Heliolisk Charizard answer but build the four around a safer Excadrill plan: do not rely on a damaged Camerupt to set up or exploit Trick Room into active Earthquake pressure, and preserve a second attacker that can pressure Excadrill without sharing the same Ground weakness. Treat Excadrill’s Focus Sash as mandatory two-hit planning. Mega Camerupt should be chosen only when Trick Room can be established with enough health and protection to give it an attack; Mega Mawile is useful for Intimidate and Armor Tail-supported priority interaction, but should not be the primary answer to an Earthquake-spamming Excadrill. Reconsider the registered six to include a non-Mega or Ground-resistant option if one from the wider roster can fill that role; available evidence is insufficient to name a definite replacement.

reflections.summary: Won the series 2-1 and Game 3 on Excadrill's Mold Breaker Earthquake OHKOing Mawile-Mega after surviving a Sucker Punch at 30%. Excadrill with Focus Sash was the correct preparation against Intimidate Mawile and was the series MVP. The opponent's Trick Room (set turn 6, three turns remaining) never fully activated because Farigiraf and Camerupt traded faints before Mawile could leverage it. Game 3 was decided by correct team preview choices (Excadrill's ability, Weavile as speed/priority) and the opponent's inability to keep Mawile-Mega healthy long enough under Trick Room. Game 1 or 2 (unseen) was lost, but the decider was controlled.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent in a rematch: (1) Reconsider Mega Charizard Y — Heliolisk will always sacrifice itself to threaten a sun-dependent sweeper; bring a lead that pressures Farigiraf instead. (2) Bring Steelix or Absol over one of Charizard/Rotom-Wash — Steelix walls Mawile-Mega's physical moves and thrives in Trick Room, Absol's Sucker Punch can punish Mawile's own Sucker Punch game. (3) Keep Excadrill with Mold Breaker and Focus Sash — it was the correct call. (4) Respect Armor Tail blocking redirection and priority moves; do not rely on Icicle Crash/VoltSwitch redirection to bypass Farigiraf. (5) Prepare for Floette-Eternal (Moonblast special wall, Flower Veil ally Defense) and Tauros-Paldea-Combat (Intimidate + Close Combat physical pressure) as potential surprise picks in a rematch.
reflections.notebook:
DURABLE NOTES — Opponent (series bf388a6d2b53):

TEAM TENDENCIES:
- Farigiraf is always the Trick Room setter (confirmed: flinched at 60% HP, consistent with Mental Herb / Helping Hand support role). Expect it every game.
- Mawile-Mega is the primary win condition. Uses Sucker Punch and PlayRough behind Helping Hand buffs. Always Mega Evolves mid-game after setup support.
- Camerupt-Mega is the Trick Room abuser (Intimidate, EarthPower/HeatWave). Enters mid-game to fire under Trick Room.
- Heliolisk is a sacrificial pivot — SolarPower Thunderbolt into opposing sun sweepers, then VoltSwitches out. Do not over-commit resources to it.
- Armor Tail on Farigiraf blocks redirection (Protect, Follow Me) and priority (Ice Shard). Sucker Punch failed against it in Trick Room — likely redirected, not a true miss.

UNBROUGHT PICKS:
- Floette-Eternal (Moonblast, EnergyBall, HelpingHand, FlowerVeil) — likely held for Fairy-type matchups or Trick Room Defense.
- Tauros-Paldea-Combat (CloseCombat, Intimidate) — likely held to punish physical attackers like Excadrill.

WHAT WORKED FOR ME:
- Excadrill Mold Breaker completely negated Intimidate from Mawile, preserving Attack for OHKOs. Correct ability read.
- Focus Sash on Excadrill guaranteed a hit after Farigiraf's faints.
- Weavile applied early pressure and forced the opponent to respect speed control.

WHAT TO FIX:
- Mega Charizard Y was dead weight — lost turn 1 to Heliolisk predictably. Need a more resilient or threatening lead.
- Rotom-Wash contributed little before collateral EQ damage. Consider replacing with Steelix (Trick Room wall) or Absol (priority counter to Mawile).
- No reliable way to break through Farigiraf + Helping Hand Mawile without Excadrill. Need a second breaker or status (Will-O-Wisp, Toxic) plan.
- Scizor was never brought — Bullet Punch in Trick Room could have threatened Mawile, but Excadrill filled the role. Scizor remains a flex pick for sun matchups.

PREP VERDICT: 4/6 correct. Excadrill and Weavile were right calls. Charizard and Rotom-Wash should be swapped for better Trick Room resilience and Mawile-Mega answers.
